headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: unstructured can read/write files and egress, while awesome-prompts is a prompt repository that may be fed into it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt/content repository, and unstructured reads documents/files by default. If awesome-prompts content is ingested into unstructured, prompt-like text can be treated as data and influence downstream processing. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is passed into unstructured as document text
IF downstream parsing treats embedded instructions as authoritative
mitigations: Add a one-line provenance label before ingestion
Strip instruction-like sections from inputs
Review a sample output for instruction-following behavior
Use a separate staging folder for prompt corpora
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured can read files and has allowlisted network egress, so any sensitive documents it processes may be transmitted to external services or logs. awesome-prompts itself is not sensitive, but if it is co-located with private documents in a shared workspace, the pair creates a realistic leakage path from files into networked processing.
conditions: IF sensitive documents share the same workspace as awesome-prompts inputs
IF unstructured sends extracted content to an allowlisted external API
mitigations: Separate public prompt repos from private document folders
Disable network egress for the processing job
Inspect allowlist destinations before running
Process a redacted sample first
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write surface, while unstructured can write files and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct write-write collision, but if both are orchestrated over the same directory, unstructured's filesystem writes can overwrite or race with operator-managed prompt assets. Uncertainty is limited, but the shared workspace risk is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF unstructured writes derived artifacts back into the source tree
mitigations: Use separate input and output directories
Mount the prompt repo read-only
Run unstructured in a temp directory
Check for unexpected file creation after a test run
requires-engineering: add locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt text that unstructured may consume as input, and unstructured can then emit parsed outputs that operators may trust. Because there is no documented verification step between them, errors or misleading instructions can cascade from content selection into downstream document processing decisions.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes outputs derived from awesome-prompts without review
IF operators act on extracted results as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Compare outputs against a known-good sample
Log source filenames alongside extracted text
Reject inputs containing imperative language
requires-engineering: add validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-prompts, and unstructured exposes privacy-policy and docs endpoints but no explicit compliance gap in the profile. The only concrete issue is that unstructured processes documents and may touch external APIs, so compliance risk is limited and not clearly pair-specific.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through unstructured
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention behavior
mitigations: Review the privacy policy before use
Avoid regulated data in test runs
Keep a local-only sample workflow
Record retention expectations in the runbook
requires-engineering: formal compliance review
